v1-01.text: Minor Hotels is one of the world's fastest-growing hospitality groups. But its next breakthrough won't be a building. It'll be a platform.

v1-02.text: Today: five hundred and ninety hotels, across sixty-three countries, on six continents. The plan — one thousand properties by twenty twenty-nine, and eighty percent of that growth is asset-light.

v1-03.text: Growth at that speed only works if every new hotel can plug in fast. And right now, it can't.

v1-04.text: Because behind every property sits the same problem: twelve or more disconnected systems. Oracle. S-A-P. Salesforce. Jira. A separate login for every one.

v1-05.text: Every task means hunting for the right tool. Every new hotel means wiring all twelve together — a process that takes months, not days.

v1-06.text: So staff work around it, running guest requests through personal WhatsApp and public A-I, outside anything secure or on-brand.

v1-07.text: And the industry has noticed. Marriott is spending one-point-one billion dollars to replatform. Wyndham's franchise portal drove ninety-six percent retention. And Mews, valued at two-point-five billion, is coming for independent hotels.

v1-08.text: The math is simple. If Minor doesn't unify its own systems, someone else will sell that unity to its franchisees.

v1-09.text: So what if all twelve systems spoke one language? Meet Meridian.

v1-10.text: Meridian is a single intelligence layer that sits on top of everything Minor already owns. One login. One portal. Every legacy system still running underneath, untouched.

v1-11.text: Ask it for last month's P and L and today's V-I-P arrivals, and it gathers both — across Oracle, the property system, and loyalty — in seconds. Ask once. It finds everything.

v1-12.text: High impact. Light lift. No rip-and-replace. This is how Minor scales to a thousand hotels, and the moment to build it is now.

v1-13.text: Meridian. The intelligence layer for Minor's asset-light future.

v2-01.text: You've seen the problem: twelve systems, twelve logins, months to onboard a single hotel. This is the answer. This is Meridian.

v2-02.text: It starts with one identity. A single secure login replaces all twelve, for every Minor hotel, owner, and operating partner.

v2-03.text: Inside is the command center. Revenue, occupancy, tonight's V-I-P arrivals, live operations — the entire property on one calm surface.

v2-04.text: And every legacy system from before? Still here — quietly connected in the sidebar, feeding Meridian in real time. Nothing was ripped out.

v2-05.text: At its heart is conversational A-I. Ask it anything — last month's P and L, today's arrivals — and it answers instantly, from across every system.

v2-06.text: But it doesn't just answer. It acts. A guest in room two-oh-three reports the air conditioning isn't cooling. One request opens the work order, dispatches engineering, and drafts the guest's apology — three systems, one approval.

v2-07.text: One ask. Three systems. Zero tabs. The complexity simply disappears.

v2-08.text: And Meridian follows the work — the front desk, the housekeeping cart, the general manager's office. Every role, every device, one platform.

v2-09.text: Underneath, it unifies six service domains: distribution, guest and loyalty, finance, workforce, brand standards, and procurement — into a single operator surface.

v2-10.text: And it's built to grow four ways — Owned, Managed, Franchise, or Affiliate. The deeper the relationship, the deeper the integration. But everyone gets the same premium Meridian.

v2-11.text: So a new franchisee keeps their existing property system and still goes live on day one. Distribution, loyalty, and brand standards, switched on in days, not months.

v2-12.text: That is how five hundred and ninety hotels becomes one thousand. Anantara, Avani, Tivoli, N-H, Oaks, and more — all under one intelligent surface.

v2-13.text: Meridian. The intelligence layer of Minor Hotels.
